chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام saying: The woman in nifas remains seated for nineteen nights; then if she sees blood, she does as the mustahadah does.
And we have also narrated from Ibn Sinan that which conflicts with this report: that the days of nifas are like the days of hayd. Thus, the two reports are in conflict.

key_terms.تِسْعَ عَشْرَةَ لَيْلَةً: nineteen nights as the stated period in this report
key_terms.دَمًا: blood seen after the stated nifas period
key_terms.ٱلنُّفَسَاءُ: a woman in the state of postnatal bleeding
key_terms.ٱلنِّفَاسِ: postnatal bleeding and its legal duration
key_terms.ٱلْحَيْضِ: menstruation, used here as a comparison for legal duration
key_terms.ٱلْخَبَرَانِ: the two reports that are said to conflict
key_terms.ٱلْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing irregular non-menstrual bleeding whose rulings then apply

ai.seo_question: What does al-Istibsar narrate about the maximum number of days of nifas?
ai.summary: This report states a legal ruling on the maximum period of nifas, mentioning nineteen nights, after which continued bleeding is treated like istihadah. It also notes a conflicting narration from Ibn Sinan equating the days of nifas with the days of hayd, indicating a jurisprudential tension between the two reports.
